title: Sednit_Xagent_Incident_Response_aab
description: Investigate and respond to a Sednit Xagent malware incident on the network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The organization has detected potential malicious activity on its network. As an incident responder, your task is to investigate and respond to this activity. The Sednit group is known for using the Xagent backdoor malware, which is capable of establishing command and control (C2) communication, lateral movement, and data exfiltration. You will need to identify services and timers as part of your investigation.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.
levels.local_content: Access the target host (IP: 192.168.50.5) using the provided credentials. Enter the word 'start' to progress to the next level.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: While monitoring network traffic, you noticed unusual outbound connections from the target host. Investigate this activity and identify the suspicious service name responsible for these connections. The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: Use the command `netstat -tuln` to identify the suspicious service name 'lab-checkin.service'. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate network connections to identify suspicious services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use network-related commands to find the suspicious service name.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run `netstat -tuln` to list all network connections and identify the suspicious service name.

levels.title: Analyze Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Now that you've identified the suspicious service, determine how it maintains persistence on the system. This will help in planning the removal of the malware. Identify the timer name responsible for persistence. The flag type is a timer name.
levels.solution: Use the command `systemctl list-timers` to identify the timer name 'lab-checkin.timer'. The flag type is a timer name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate systemd timers to determine the persistence mechanism.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use systemd-related commands to find the timer name.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run `systemctl list-timers` to list all systemd timers and identify the timer name.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: The Sednit group is known for moving laterally within compromised networks. Investigate if the malware has attempted to move laterally from the target host to other systems in the network. Identify the service name responsible for lateral movement. The flag type is a service name.
levels.solution: Use the command `ps aux` to identify the service name 'payload-transfer.service'. The flag type is a service name.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Investigate running processes to identify evidence of lateral movement.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use process-related commands to find the service name.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run `ps aux` to list all running processes and identify the service name.
